column1: # Level-1 route manifest (issue #24). One file per level drives `route-gate.ps1` and the replay's
# `--route-trace` columns; the gate and the app hold no level literal of their own.
# Rows are tab-separated: a key, then its values. `#` starts a comment.
#   level <name>                     the level the replay boots (`--start`)
#   port <path>                      the committed port-side oracle (graded on every row)
#   retail <path> <warp>             optional retail prefix, graded on the rows before the plan's
#                                    first warp named <warp> (the port-only segment starts there)
#   mechanics <name>...              the mechanics the provenance file must cover
#   prereq <gate.ps1>                a gate that must pass before this verdict counts
#   use <thing>                      the replay's use trace must name this linked thing
#   after_use <column>               the event reads 0 at and before the plan's first use tick
#   cross <column> <axis> <value>    after the event latched, some sample past the first use has
#   final <column> <value>           the trace's last row carries this value
# Read by the app (`--route-manifest`), in trace-column order after `health`/`shields`:
#   watch <column> <cog> <symbol>    placed cog <cog>'s variable <symbol>, `-` until the cog starts
#   latch <column> <watch>...        1 from the first sample where any named watch reads non-zero
# Every `latch`/`bin`/`level_end` column is a latched event: the retail prefix grades it on its last
# row only, the port oracle on every row.

# placed cog 11). Their symbol names differ (`opendoors` vs `open_doors`).
